top: Indians moved above the World Bank's $4.20-a-day poverty line between 2011-12 and 2023-24.
India's Gini index on consumption (World Bank, 2023) against income (World Inequality Database, 2023).

sections.h2: Share below the $4.20-a-day line fell from 57.7% to 16.1% in twelve years

chart.title: The $4.20-a-day poverty rate fell by more than half from 2011-12 to 2023-24
chart.sub: Share of Indians below the $4.20-a-day line, %.

sections.means: The share below the $4.20 line fell from 57.7% to 16.1%, which the World Bank says moved about 496 million people above it.
sections.todo: Lead with the twelve-year change and report it as the World Bank's estimate rather than as a settled figure.

sections.h2: The $4.20 rate fell by a third in 2023-24 alone, a change the World Bank urges caution on

chart.title: The $4.20 rate fell from 23.9% to 16.1% in one survey year
chart.sub: Share of Indians below the $4.20-a-day line, %.

sections.means: The $4.20 rate fell by 33% in 2023-24, and the World Bank says it cannot yet separate real gains from better recording.
sections.todo: Quote the one-year drop only with the World Bank's caveat that it should not be read in isolation.

sections.h2: The same country reads 23 on consumption and 62 on income, a gap about the survey

chart.title: The same country reads 23 on consumption and 62 on income
chart.sub: Gini index, 0 = everyone equal, 100 = one person has everything.
chart.source: World Bank (consumption; PLFS earnings); World Inequality Database via World Bank.

sections.means: India's consumption Gini of 23 is far below its income Gini of 62, and the post says the gap reflects what the survey reaches.
sections.todo: Compare inequality only within one measure, and say which survey each Gini comes from.

sections.h2: Rs 100 crore-plus filers rose 46% in 2024-25 as survey top spending fell

chart.title: Rs 100 crore-plus filers rose 46% in 2024-25 as survey top spending fell
chart.sub: People reporting gross total income of Rs 100 crore or more, by assessment year.
chart.source: Ministry of Finance reply to Lok Sabha unstarred question 1274, 27 July 2026.

sections.means: The number of people reporting Rs 100 crore or more rose from 284 to 415 between 2023-24 and 2024-25, a rise of 46%.
sections.todo: Set the tax count beside the survey's top-end spending so readers can see the two measures pointing in opposite directions.
